source.excerpt: human history began with an act of disobedience
trail: The CUNY English Department teaching PDF reproduces the essay opening and credits Fromm.
Its bibliographic note identifies a 1984 collection edition and says the essay was first published in 1963. Wikiquote separately locates it in On Disobedience and Other Essays (1981).
This verifies the sentence in Fromm’s text, rather than claiming that this teaching transcription is a 1963 facsimile.

Rainer Funk’s literary-estate catalogue, p.83, entry 1963d-000-eng, independently places the essay in A Matter of Life (London: Jonathan Cape, 1963), pp.97–105. This identifies publication, not where Fromm composed the text.

author.heading: About Erich Fromm
author.bio: Erich Fromm (1900–1980) was a German-American social psychologist and psychoanalyst associated with the Frankfurt School. A refugee from Nazi Germany, he helped found the William Alanson White Institute in New York; his books connect individual character with the pressures of social life.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Fromm reads the stories of Adam and Eve and Prometheus as myths about independence achieved through disobedience. He then turns to the Atomic Age: obedience to orders could enable humanity’s destruction. The essay also explicitly rejects the idea that all disobedience is good or all obedience bad.
